title: John Calvin
source: Public domain. Consolidated from John Calvin, Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans, translated by John Owen, Calvin Translation Society, and the Institutes of the Christian Religion, translated by Henry Beveridge; both as published by the Christian Classics Ethereal Library.
body: John Calvin on Romans, chapter 7. In his Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans, in the John Owen translation, Calvin writes at Romans 7, verse 1: Though he had, in a brief manner, sufficiently explained the question respecting the abrogation of the law; yet as it was a difficult one, and might have given rise to many other questions, he now shows more at large how the law, with regard to us, is become abrogated; and then he sets forth what good is thereby done to us: for while it holds us separated from Christ and bound to itself, it can do nothing but condemn us. In the Institutes of the Christian Religion, in the Henry Beveridge translation, Calvin draws on this chapter again in Book 2, chapter 2.
